title: Quasi-excellence is preserved by locally finite-type morphisms
statement: Let $h:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Assume that every affine open of $Y$ has quasi-excellent coordinate ring [def-exc-excellent-ring]. Then every affine open of $X$ has quasi-excellent coordinate ring as well. If $X$ is quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme], then $X$ is Noetherian: it has a finite affine open cover whose coordinate rings are Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. No finite-dimensionality or universal catenarity hypothesis is imposed.
